title: Novel Factory unified temporal read and concurrent acceptance contracts 2.1
description: Design contracts. Core 2.0 is preserved byte-for-byte. Structural validity is not authorization, reference validity, schedule completeness or verified database concurrency.

KnowledgeCut.description: A requested view, not authorization. The server checks every actor, time, manifest and reader cut against the current task grant.

ReadContract.description: World evaluation and index freshness are independent. WAIT observes existing authorized advance work only; a fixed revision cannot acquire later world events.

ResolvedReadCut.description: One immutable cut for all subqueries; permission is rechecked on delivery. Permission epoch is an opaque monotonic grant marker, not a hidden-scope count.

ValidityInterval.description: Open end means no selected closing transition, not that the world has been evaluated forever. Bounded query intervals still use core StoryInterval.

RelationTransition.description: OPEN creates a new relation occurrence ID; CLOSE names its selected projection version. Close then reopen uses a new relation_id. at must be a proved effective boundary, never a guessed endpoint of uncertain occurrence time. Registered domain predicates, cardinality and source events are checked by services.

TemporalRelationRecord.description: Read-only projection of selected accepted effects or accepted belief records. BELIEF describes what an actor believes, not objective truth. It is not a second writable assertion store. Knowledge views may expose only authorized source evidence.

TemporalEntry.description: Read-only normalization across typed stores. An accepted promise is a fact about speech, not proof of its target outcome. Summary text has no write authority.

TypedStateAnswer.description: R1 narrows the legacy data field to typed state values; each subject/predicate receives its own knowledge/evaluation/coverage status.

QueryBatchRequest.description: Read-only, one principal/task/view and one resolved cut. Predicates and per-item plane compatibility are checked as in UnifiedQueryRequest. Item IDs are unique. Enforce an aggregate cost budget, not just 32 items.

ContextCompileRequest.description: The resolved WorldRef must equal the immutable TaskSpec input for this generation. A different dynamic cut returns TASK_REBIND_REQUIRED; the control plane creates a new input/generation. Missing ContextBundle does not authorize rewriting TaskSpec. Recipes and budgets never grant privileges.

CompiledContext.description: A compiler receipt accompanies the existing core bundle ID. All primary/auxiliary cuts use the same WorldRef and independently authorized source manifests. Every section is authorized; required constraints are never silently truncated. Omitted labels are sanitized.

ScopeToken.description: Internal server-owned monotonic token. Never expose secret scope identifiers to restricted roles; provide opaque dependency handles. Parent registry guards detect creation; tombstones prevent ABA.

ApprovalBinding.description: Server-issued policy binding. Legacy approvals default STRICT_BASE. A caller cannot mark its own approval DEPENDENCY_STABLE.

AcceptanceCertificate.description: Trusted immutable certificate, not an LLM claim. Commit checks server provenance, same history, current task/grant, all guards, actual closure and current domain invariants. Unrelated HEAD movement alone may preserve eligibility.

GuardedAcceptRequest.description: Exact request hash remains fixed across retry; actual parent comes from the transaction. STRICT_HEAD requires actual parent=base. New certificates use new command keys, with target/proposal uniqueness preventing a second effect.

AcceptedEventR1.description: R1 normalized event payload; accepted authority still requires branch selection and formal commit. Each legacy/new effect normalizes into one canonical projection slot; duplicates are domain errors.

WorldChangeSetR1.description: Versioned extension of the same selection/commit mechanism. Runtime relation/state changes are event effects, not arbitrary ASSERTION writes. Existing record operations retain original restricted semantics.
